headline: FOMC WEEK: WARSH'S FIRST DOT PLOT JUNE 17 — Gold at $4,195 Heads Into Metals Market's Binary Moment
snippet: Gold at $4,195/oz enters the most consequential week of H1 2026 as Kevin Warsh chairs his inaugural FOMC meeting on June 16–17 — the first Fed meeting under the new Chair whose monetary instincts the market has not yet fully priced. A rate hold is 97% odds, but what the dot plot signals about the trajectory of rates under a supply-shock inflation regime (May CPI 4.2%, driven by Strait of Hormuz oil disruptions) will determine whether gold reasserts its structural bid toward $5,000+ or revisits the $4,150 support level. Gold has already absorbed two stacked bearish catalysts — hot PPI plus the ECB rate hike — and held above $4,150. Whether that resilience translates into a recovery or another leg lower depends entirely on Warsh's framing of what kind of inflation the Fed is fighting. For junior mining investors, this week's FOMC communication is a direct read-through to commodity equity valuations, junior project financing costs, and the pace of gold sector M&A that has accelerated throughout Q1 and Q2 2026.

headline: GDX -13%, GDXJ -15% FROM 2026 HIGHS — Mining Experts Diagnose Capitulation as Pre-Rally Buy Signal
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) has shed approximately 13% from its 2026 highs and the junior-focused GDXJ has fallen 15–18%, as hawkish Fed fears — amplified by Warsh's unknown monetary instincts, Iran-driven oil above $100, and May CPI at 4.2% — triggered sector-wide institutional de-risking ahead of the June 16–17 FOMC. Mining sector analysts argue the capitulation pattern — equities selling hard while physical gold holds $4,150+ — mirrors the classic pre-rally template where miners discount a macro scenario (sustained rate hikes) that the physical market is not pricing in. The gold-to-GDX ratio has widened to historically stretched levels comparable to late 2022 and mid-2024, both of which were followed by violent mean-reversion rallies in mining equities within 60 days. With all-in sustaining costs running $1,200–$1,400/oz against a $4,195 spot price, gold miner operating margins are at multi-decade highs — yet equity valuations are near cycle lows. That disconnect, analysts argue, is what institutional rotations historically correct quickly once the macro uncertainty catalyst resolves.

headline: ENERGY FUELS HITS FULL-YEAR URANIUM GUIDANCE AT HALFWAY MARK — 1.6M lbs U3O8 By June 30 at $9-12/lb Mill Cost
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU; TSX: EFR) announced June 11 that it expects to produce approximately 1.6 million pounds of finished U3O8 from January through June 2026 — placing the company within its full-year guidance range of 1.5 to 2.5 million pounds at the exact halfway mark of the year. Mining and processing costs at the Pinyon Plain Mine are tracking at $23–$30 per pound, while White Mesa Mill's processing cost has reached a historic low of $9–$12 per pound of U3O8. Uranium ore processing at the mill is expected to complete by end of June to rebuild ore stockpiles, with the mill resuming U3O8 production in Q4 2026. At spot uranium near $85/lb, Pinyon Plain's all-in cost structure implies a 100%+ operating margin on processed material. Hitting full-year guidance at midyear gives Energy Fuels full H2 optionality to pursue vanadium recovery, rare earth processing from monazite concentrate, and additional uranium commitments to its growing US government utility customer base — making this an execution milestone with positive read-throughs for the broader US uranium production sector.

headline: VISIBLE GOLD IN ALL THREE HOLES: Metals Creek Completes Ogden Drill — Deep 350m Intercept on Timmins Fault
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Metals Creek Resources
snippet: Metals Creek Resources Corp. (TSXV: MEK) announced June 11 that all three holes completed at the Ogden Gold Project in Timmins, Ontario have intersected visible gold — including final hole TOG-26-77, which hit visible gold at 350.36 metres depth within altered felsite on the Thomas Ogden Zone fold structure. The Ogden project is a 50/50 joint venture with Discovery Silver, operated by Metals Creek, located 6 km south of Timmins on 8 kilometres of the prolific Porcupine-Destor Fault — host to multiple former producing mines. Assay results from all three holes are pending, and a 100% visible gold hit rate on a reconnaissance program targeting deeper structural extensions provides a compelling setup ahead of those assays. In the context of gold at $4,195/oz and the Timmins-Porcupine camp commanding premium acquisition multiples from mid-tier producers seeking bolt-on production in Ontario, a three-hole program with a clean hit rate on an 8-km fault segment with substantial untested strike represents the early-stage exploration footprint that draws follow-up capital.

headline: ZIJIN/ALLIED GOLD IN LIMBO: NDRC STALL FORCES JULY 29 EXTENSION — C$5.5B Africa Deal Trades 21% Below Offer
snippet: Zijin Gold International's C$5.5 billion (approximately US$4 billion) all-cash acquisition of Allied Gold Corp. (TSX: AAUC) at C$44 per share has been extended a second time to July 29, 2026, after China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) delayed final approval — the last outstanding regulatory hurdle. The NDRC's reported concerns centre on the transaction premium and political risk in Allied's asset portfolio: the Sadiola Gold Mine in Mali, the Bonikro-Agbaou complex in Côte d'Ivoire, and the Kurmuk Gold Mine in Ethiopia. Allied's shares were trading at approximately C$34.73 as of early June — a persistent 21% discount to the C$44 offer price — signalling that institutional arbitrageurs are pricing a meaningful probability of deal failure or forced renegotiation. For junior gold sector investors, the delayed close has kept a C$5.5 billion capital slug in limbo that, upon closing or collapse, would immediately trigger a redeployment event across the African and global mid-tier gold sector.

headline: SILVER ENTERS FOMC WEEK AT $64.50 — Sixth Straight Supply Deficit + COMEX Squeeze Fuel Bank $300 Targets
snippet: Silver is trading at $64.50 per ounce heading into FOMC week after a 10%+ pullback from its 2026 highs, with the gold-silver ratio re-expanding toward 65 — a level that historically marks late-stage corrections within secular precious metals bull markets. The Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 projects the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of approximately 46 million ounces, with cumulative above-ground stock drawdowns since 2021 now approaching 762 million ounces. COMEX silver inventories have declined materially as solar photovoltaic manufacturing, EV battery contacts, and AI data centre electrical infrastructure continue to drive industrial fabrication demand independently of investment sentiment. Bank of America, Citigroup, and Reuters-consensus analysts have published silver price targets ranging from $200 to $300 for 2026–2027, citing the structural deficit compounded by China's classification of silver as a strategic material since January 1, 2026 requiring export licences. For junior silver miners and primary silver explorers, a recovery from current levels toward any portion of bank consensus targets would represent one of the most powerful commodity price tailwinds in current markets.

headline: 10,000m UNDERWAY IN BC: Brixton Metals Spuds Thorn Copper-Gold Porphyry Program, Northwest British Columbia
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation (TSXV: BBB) announced the commencement of its fully funded 10,000-metre 2026 exploration program at the Thorn Project in northwestern British Columbia — a copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry and epithermal system in BC's Golden Triangle, one of Canada's highest-concentration districts for significant mineral discoveries. The program is Brixton's largest single-season commitment at Thorn, building on a substantial historical database and targeting multiple porphyry copper-gold centres within the district-scale land package. The Golden Triangle has produced some of Canada's most significant discoveries in the current cycle — including Newcrest's Brucejack mine and Seabridge Gold's KSM — with multiple TSXV explorers having attracted major mining company earn-in agreements from the same district. In a Section 232 tariff environment that has structurally elevated North American copper premiums and accelerated senior producer interest in securing allied-jurisdiction copper-gold assets ahead of the forecast 491,000-tonne annual copper deficit through 2030, a fully funded 10,000-metre Golden Triangle porphyry program represents well-timed capital deployment.

headline: MORGAN STANLEY: FOUR STRUCTURAL PILLARS MEAN WARSH WON'T KILL THE PRECIOUS METALS BULL — Stay Long
snippet: Morgan Stanley's precious metals strategy team, as reported by Canadian Mining Report, argues that Kevin Warsh's appointment as Federal Reserve Chair does not alter the four structural pillars driving the current precious metals bull: (1) central bank gold buying at historically elevated annual rates — 850 tonnes purchased in 2025 alone; (2) fiscal expansion and debt monetisation concerns unresolvable by any single Fed Chair appointment; (3) de-dollarisation momentum among emerging market economies diversifying reserves away from US Treasuries; and (4) supply-shock inflation driven by energy prices — a dynamic that raising rates amplifies rather than cures by raising the cost of oil infrastructure investment needed to resolve the underlying supply crisis. Morgan Stanley's conclusion is that Warsh faces a stagflation-adjacent dilemma with no clean policy response, and that precious metals retain their structural bid regardless of his rate stance. For investors who sold miners on Warsh appointment risk, the bank frames the sell-off as a mischaracterised risk event and an entry opportunity rather than a regime change.

headline: KIA CONTROLS HALF THE WORLD'S TERBIUM AND DYSPROSIUM — Myanmar HREE Crisis Deepens as Military Offensives Escalate
snippet: The Kachin Independence Army (KIA) retook operational control of Myanmar's primary heavy rare earth extraction zones in Chipwi and Pangwa townships in October 2024 and has maintained that control through continuing military offensives as of May–June 2026. Myanmar's ion-adsorption clay deposits in Kachin and Shan States account for approximately two-thirds of the terbium and dysprosium processed in China — which itself controls over 90% of global HREE refining capacity — making the ongoing conflict a direct supply chain event for EV motor manufacturers, wind turbine producers, and defence contractors dependent on high-performance permanent magnets. Chinese customs data shows HREE export volumes from Myanmar remain below pre-seizure levels despite a December 2024 trade arrangement with the KIA. Some industry sources argue that for dysprosium and terbium specifically, physical access has decoupled from price — supply is simply unavailable at any price in spot markets — a condition that significantly favours the small number of Western junior explorers advancing HREE projects in non-Chinese, non-Myanmar jurisdictions.

headline: DIOS EXPLORATION WRAPS AU33 GOLD DRILL PROGRAM, QUEBEC — 10 Holes Over 2,024m Target Heberto Zone Extension
snippet: Dios Exploration Inc. (TSXV: DOS) announced the completion of its 2026 follow-up diamond drilling program on the AU33 Gold Project in Quebec — 10 holes covering 2,024 metres, with 9 of the 10 holes targeting extensions of the Heberto Gold Zone and 1 hole testing a newly identified geophysical target. The program follows up on the discovery of the Heberto Gold Zone during the prior drilling season and, now complete, positions Dios for an assay-results release that will define grade and geometry in sufficient detail for resource estimation planning. The AU33 project is located in the Chibougamau-Chapais mining region, a historically productive Quebec gold district with established infrastructure and First Nations partnership frameworks. At $4,195/oz gold, a drill-complete program on a discovery zone in a proven Quebec district represents the early-stage discovery inflection that attracts speculative capital ahead of assays — particularly for sub-C$10M market cap juniors where a single strong assay result can be a re-rating event.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER PRINT MULTI-MONTH LOWS — $4,150 IS THE LINE IN THE SAND Before FOMC; Ratio Signals Late-Stage Correction
snippet: Gold touched intraday lows of $4,130–$4,150 and silver dipped below $62 during the first two weeks of June 2026 before recovering to $4,195 and $64.50 respectively — multi-month technical lows driven by the combined weight of US-Iran conflict energy inflation, a May CPI print of 4.2% year-over-year, and deep uncertainty around incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's monetary policy instincts ahead of the June 16–17 FOMC. Technical analysts identify $4,150 as the critical gold support level: a weekly close below that level before Wednesday's FOMC would signal a deeper retest of $3,900–$4,000, while holding it — as gold has done through two tests — keeps the bullish structural case intact. The gold-silver ratio has re-expanded from its recent compression near 62:1 to approximately 65:1, a historically reliable signal of a late-stage correction within secular bull markets where silver underperforms before a sharp recovery once precious metals confidence returns — a pattern that preceded the most violent silver upside moves of the current bull cycle.
